verdict.rationale: iTerm2 ships a built-in LLM chat window that can read terminal contents. Linked sessions get context-aware help, and the chat can explain output with annotations, which matches AI insights and suggestions from the user's own data inside the product. A hands-on community report confirms it generating a working awk command. missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the insight/annotation behavior (evidence is a single README line plus a plugin blurb), and clarity on setup limits (separate AI plugin install and a user-supplied API key are required).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can get AI-generated insights and suggestions from my data inside the product

citations.quote: Built-in LLM chat window that can optionally interact with terminal contents. Link sessions to get context-aware help, run commands on your behalf, or explain output with annotations.
This is an optional component you can install to enable generative AI features in iTerm2.
One user prompted the iTerm2 AI feature to use awk to filter the 2nd and 5th columns of piped input and truncate the 5th to 25 chars.
